newsitem.title: USA: Aviron shares flat after IPO size reduced.
newsitem.headline: Aviron shares flat after IPO size reduced.

text.p: Aviron Inc shares had a flat market debut on Tuesday after the company cut back terms of its initial public offering by more than 50 percent.
Aviron, which focuses on disease prevention, was flat at $8. It offered two million shares in the $16 million offering.

The company had filed in early June for an IPO of three million shares to price between about $11 and $13 per share, which would have raised about $36 million, but put the offering on hold due to market conditions.
Robertson Stephens & Co was the lead manager of the deal.

Concurrent with the offering, Aviron said it plans to sell 222,222 shares of its common stock to Sang-A Pharm Co Ltd in a private placement at the IPO price of $8, with the number of shares to be sold to Sang-A subject to adjustment under certain conditions.

Aviron is currently conducting a Phase III clinical trial in children of its live cold adapted intranasal vaccine for influenza, and has recently announced results from a challenge efficacy study in healthy adults for this vaccine.
